name: Cabaret Voltaire
label: Rough Trade
lede: Three Sheffield friends played tape loops of steam hammers out of the back of a van, got beaten up at their first gig, and spent the next twenty years turning that noise into music people could dance to.

eras.title: Steam hammers in a Totley attic
eras.text: Chris Watson was a Post Office telephone engineer who wanted music without instruments; Richard H. Kirk took to heart Brian Eno's line that you didn't need to be a musician. They named the band after the Zürich club where Dada started, and treated Sheffield as the audience whether it wanted to be or not.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary · The Quietus: The Strange World Of
years.h: Watson and Kirk start making tape loops; Mallinder brings a bass
years.p: Watson's attic in Totley becomes the lab: a reel-to-reel, mail-order oscillators, Kirk's clarinet and guitar. Late in 1973 Kirk's friend [[Stephen Mallinder|adad4d39-c1e6-4533-b4dc-76e6ac328299]] joins on bass and vocals.
years.xp:
Mallinder on the name: "The whole Dada thing was always a touchstone for us." They borrowed a VCS3 synth from Sheffield University's music department until Watson built his own.

Kirk and Mallinder had been going to soul nights since they were 13. Kirk's steelworker father, a radio ham, got him into electronics.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: Tape loops out of a van, and weird noise in the pubs
years.p: The trio drive Sheffield with loops playing from loudspeakers on a friend's van roof, and play tapes in public toilets and pubs.
years.xp: Kirk to Bandcamp Daily: "We'd do mad stuff, drive around in a van with tape loops playing out the back, or go into pubs with a tape machine and play weird stuff. Just trying to wind people up."

years.src: The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: Billed as a funk band, the first gig ends with Mallinder in hospital
years.p: They talk their way onto a Tuesday disco night by claiming to play funk. The audience invades the stage and beats them up.
years.xp:
Watson described the set: a tape loop of a steam hammer for percussion, and Kirk playing a clarinet in a rubberised jacket strung with flashing fairy lights.

It wasn't the last time. At another show Mallinder was hospitalised with a chipped backbone after the crowd started throwing things.

years.cap: Kirk, Mallinder and Watson in Sheffield
years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Western Works opens on Portobello Street
years.p: Watson pays for a studio on the second floor of a building in Sheffield, once the offices of the Sheffield Federation of Young Socialists. [[The Human League|7adaabfb-acfb-47bc-8c7c-59471c2f0db8]], Clock DVA and [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]] would all record early tracks there.

eras.title: Paid in Revox
eras.text: Punk gave them a crowd that would at least stay in the room. Rough Trade gave them a tape machine instead of an advance, and the singles and albums that followed made Sheffield sound like nowhere else.

years.src: The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Glasses fly at the Lyceum and the set gets cut short
years.p: Even punk had limits: supporting [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] in London, the band are driven off by a crowd throwing glasses.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Rough Trade signs them with a four-track Revox
years.p: Factory Records had offered, and [[Throbbing Gristle|e135d690-9c53-4333-8f11-98aec8c9f434]] wanted them for Industrial. Rough Trade won with a Revox tape machine in place of an advance.
years.xp:
NME's Andy Gill, June 27, 1978: "I firmly believe Cabaret Voltaire will turn out to be one of the most important new bands to achieve wider recognition this year. Wait and see."

Radio Hallam's Richard Tandy and Radio 1's [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] were early champions.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Extended Play, with a Velvet Underground cover
years.p: The first Rough Trade record carries 'Do the Mussolini (Headkick)' and the [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]]'s 'Here She Comes Now'. Kirk called White Light/White Heat a blueprint for the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Quietus: The Strange World Of
years.h: 'Nag Nag Nag' gets bad reviews and sells 10,000
years.p: The single makes the indie chart and travels to France and Belgium. Decades later, at the reunion, nobody could find the drum machine it was made on.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Mix-Up, the first album, out on Rough Trade
years.p: Recorded at Western Works and released four days before the band's show at the YMCA, later issued as Live at the Y.M.C.A. 27-10-79. Mix-Up reaches No. 12 on the indie chart.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: The Voice of America loops broadcasts into the rhythm
years.p: Found sound and radio snatches over hard drum machines, years before samplers made it routine. It reaches No. 3 on the indie chart.
play: The Voice of America/Damage Is Done

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Red Mecca goes to No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: The last album with the original trio. Bandcamp Daily files it with Mix-Up and The Voice of America as the austere industrial funk of their first run.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Quietus: The Strange World Of
years.h: Watson leaves for a job at Tyne Tees Television
years.p: Watson goes into TV sound and co-founds The Hafler Trio, then becomes the BBC wildlife recordist whose work runs through David Attenborough's films.
years.xp: A John Peel session the trio had recorded aired on June 25, 1981: 'Black Mask', 'Greensborough', 'Walls of Jericho' and 'Jazz the Glass'.

eras.title: Two men and Virgin's money
eras.text: As a duo, Kirk and Mallinder chose to go for the dancefloor on purpose. A New York remix, a £50,000 advance and a string of club records followed, and so did the strain of being an experimental band on the verge of pop.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography
years.h: Japan, Europe and the US, with no major label behind them
years.p: The duo tour without big-label support and release Hai!, recorded live in Japan. 2x45 tops the indie chart.
years.xp: On January 19, 1982, they played a benefit at Sheffield University, later released under the name Pressure Company.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: John Robie remixes 'Yashar' for Factory
years.p: [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]] introduce the band to the New York dance producer. His 12-inch of the 2x45 track gets heavy club play.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Stevo signs them to Some Bizzare for £50,000
years.p: Stevo Pearce's Some Bizzare licenses them to Virgin. The advance rebuilds Western Works; the condition is that the next album is made in London.

years.cap: Kirk and Mallinder as a duo
years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography
years.h: The Crackdown reaches No. 31, sixty places past their old best
years.p: Made with producer Flood, and with Soft Cell's Dave Ball sitting in. 'Just Fascination' becomes a club record.

q: They implied a new way of making music.
years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Peter Care's 'Sensoria' video wins the LA Times's best of 1985
years.p: The 12-inch melds two Micro-Phonies tracks, 'Sensoria' and 'Do Right', co-produced with John Potoker. Sheffield later named a festival after it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography
years.h: Drinking Gasoline, a double 12-inch spun off a videotape
years.p: It comes from Gasoline in Your Eye, a compilation of videos and footage for an unfinished film called Earthshaker. An American tour follows, then The Covenant, the Sword and the Arm of the Lord, their last for Virgin.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography
years.h: EMI money buys Adrian Sherwood for Code
years.p: With [[Bill Nelson|8d463dee-ffae-4028-a3af-ec8ccb595906]] on guitar. At home, Western Works is given up after a run of break-ins.
years.xp: Old accounting problems threatened a forced sale of their newer studio. Mallinder moved to London; Kirk stayed in Sheffield. Wikipedia describes the split as the extrovert and the reluctant one, mirroring a band on the edge of going pop.

eras.title: House music, back where it came from
eras.text: House music in Chicago had grown partly out of records like theirs. The band went to Chicago to make house, ran up debts at EMI, and wound down as Kirk drifted toward Warp and the bleep sound.

years.big: "They didn't understand that they informed house music."
years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: A month in Chicago with Marshall Jefferson
years.p: [[Ministry|13df2a46-f72f-40e7-aa63-26fcf62c7048]]'s [[Al Jourgensen|6c0dadab-266a-4601-8394-5b8e19e90def]], who worked with them in Acid Horse, on the irony. Groovy, Laidback and Nasty features Ten City and Kym Mazelle; EMI drops the band soon after.
years.xp:
They had tried and failed to reach New York's Todd Terry before an Atlantic executive introduced them to Marshall Jefferson. The single 'Hypnotised' got remixes from A Guy Called Gerald and Daniel Miller.

Mick Fish made the same point in his 1989 book: the found-vocal-over-hard-rhythm trick all over the charts was one the band had nearly invented ten years earlier.

years.src: The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Kirk's Sweet Exorcist helps define Warp's bleep sound
years.p: With Richard Barratt, Kirk releases 'Testone' and 'Clonk', among Warp Records' first. Their album was the label's first LP, in 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography
years.h: The Conversation is the last album for 26 years
years.p: One of three instrumental records from 1992 to 1994. Mallinder sang last on 1991's Body and Soul, and moves to Perth, Australia, where he starts OffWorld Sounds and an academic career.

eras.title: Kirk keeps the name
eras.text: Kirk brought back Cabaret Voltaire as a one-man operation and refused to play the old songs. He made four new records in his last two years.

years.src: The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: Kirk turns down Coachella and revives the band alone
years.p: He said no to "a very fucking large amount of money" to re-form the trio. The new Cabaret Voltaire plays no old songs.
years.xp:
To Fact in 2017: "Cabaret Voltaire was always about breaking new ground and moving forward. It would be so sad to see it as a nostalgia act."

The first revived records, made at Western Works, were collaborations with New Zealand's Kora and Sheffield's the Tivoli.

years.cap: Kirk's Cabaret Voltaire at Incubate, Tilburg
years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: Berlin Atonal: the first show in twenty years is Kirk and machines
years.p: All new material, multi-screen projections, and Kirk as the only person on stage.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire discography
years.h: Shadow of Fear, the first new album in 26 years
years.p: Out on Mute Records, led by 'Vasto'. Dekadrone, BN9Drone and the Shadow of Funk EP follow in 2021.

years.src: The Guardian: Richard H Kirk obituary
years.h: Richard H. Kirk dies at 65
years.p: A lifelong Sheffield resident who kept his private life private. Mallinder called him difficult to live with but impossible not to love.
years.xp: Beyond Cabaret Voltaire, Kirk recorded under his own name and dozens of aliases, including Sandoz, Electronic Eye and Dark Magus. [[Throbbing Gristle|e135d690-9c53-4333-8f11-98aec8c9f434]]'s Chris Carter and Cosey Fanni Tutti once got a bag of brilliant dance tracks from him and found they were all his.

eras.title: Fifty years on, for Richard Kirk
eras.text: Mallinder and Watson had not played as Cabaret Voltaire since 1981. They came back for the band's fiftieth anniversary in a Sheffield forge, then booked a farewell tour.

years.cap: Cabaret Voltaire at FORGE, Sheffield, October 25, 2025
years.src: The Quietus: An Elated Sense of Unity · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
yt: Full set at XOYO, Birmingham, November 19, 2025
years.h: Mallinder opens the Sheffield reunion with three words: "For Richard Kirk"
years.p: At the Sensoria festival, in a former Victorian steel forge, with Eric Random on guitar. The set runs from 'The Voice of America' to 'Nag Nag Nag' and closes on 'Sensoria'.
years.xp: Watson worked in his own 2012 recording of Sheffield's Tinsley Viaduct, which The Quietus heard as deep musique concrète of drones and steam-like hisses. Oliver Harrap of the Moonlandingz stood in on drums at short notice for Benge.

years.src: Brooklyn Vegan · Wikipedia: Cabaret Voltaire
years.h: A final tour, ending where it started
years.p: Europe, North America and the UK, set to finish on October 25, 2026, at the Octagon in Sheffield. A live album from the tour is announced in February.
